source: USGS Water Services instantaneous-values API (waterservices.usgs.gov/nwis/iv), keyless — 14 live-verified gauges on the Mississippi barge corridor + Ohio/Missouri/Illinois tributaries (dead Metropolis gauge 03611500 excluded)
license: USGS data are public domain (U.S. Government work). Provisional readings subject to revision. Attribution: 'Data courtesy U.S. Geological Survey'.

field_map.name: gauge site name
field_map.param: 00065 gage height ft (primary) | 00060 discharge ft3/s (Memphis + Vicksburg publish discharge only — verified)
field_map.v: reading value (numeric; unit implied by param; USGS -999999 sentinels dropped)
field_map.rt: as-seen date (UTC day WE fetched it)

confidence_model: provisional (q=P) values revise to approved (A); a revision appends a NEW row (same site+param+d, new v/q, new rt) — point-in-time vintage like fredmacro. The low-water SIGNAL interpretation (barge stress) is gate-2-locked and never surfaced from this raw record.
cadence: 1h poll; one request covers all sites; dedup by site|param|d|v|q
_note: Universal archive envelope (approved 2026-07-04): dataset-level manifest; datum-level fields where information varies per record. Append-only JSONL unless stated; readers pick field_map from here. Gauges are map-plottable — /data registry layer ships with this stream.
